subject: MAP: benchmarking scope & success criteria - latency/throughput/TTFT
messages:
From: Karthish Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eli Tanner <eli.tanner@acmecorp.com>, Samira Gomez <samira.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: benchmarking scope & success criteria - latency/throughput/TTFT

Hi Eli / Samira,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the clear timeline. Per our mutual action plan (MAP) I put together an initial benchmarking scope so we can align on what success looks like for the PoC. High-level goals: measure tail latency (95th/99th), median TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput at target concurrency, and error/retry behavior under a realistic prompt mix.

Draft plan attached (redwood-map-benchmark-plan-v1.xlsx). Key asks from Acme: share representative prompt set (10–15 templates + token length distribution) and a target concurrency profile (spikes vs sustained).

Proposed success criteria (suggestions):
- 95th-token-latency < 250 ms for single-region hosted mode at 8k context
- TTFT median < 100 ms across representative prompts
- Sustained throughput of 120 requests/min with <1% 5xx errors
- Graceful degradation: when capacity saturated, fallback latency increase <2x and error rate <5%

Can you confirm you can provide the prompt corpus and target traffic windows by Tue (5/5)? If so we can run a three-day load window next week and share results on Fri.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-map-benchmark-plan-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Eli Tanner <eli.tanner@acmecorp.com>
To: Karthish Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Gomez <samira.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: benchmarking scope & success criteria - latency/throughput/TTFT

On Sun, May 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM Karthish Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Draft plan attached (redwood-map-benchmark-plan-v1.xlsx). Key asks from Acme: share representative prompt set (10–15 templates + token length distribution) and a target concurrency profile (spikes vs sustained).

Thanks Karthik — this looks sensible. We can provide the prompt templates and a week's historical traffic profile (anonymized) by end of day Tue (5/5). Regarding success criteria, two points from our side:

- For a production cutover we'll need consistent 95th percentile <300 ms across a mixed workload (some templates generate longer outputs). Can you include per-template breakdowns?
- We also need a short-run reproducibility check (same inputs over 50 runs) to ensure determinism within acceptable variance (stdev of latency <15%).

We'll aim to run the earliest load window on Wed (5/6) if that works for you.

—Eli
Senior Engineering Manager, Acme Corp
From: Karthish Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eli Tanner <eli.tanner@acmecorp.com>, Samira Gomez <samira.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: benchmarking scope & success criteria - latency/throughput/TTFT

Appreciate the notes, Eli — yes we can: per-template latency breakdowns and a reproducibility batch (50 runs) will be part of the runbook. Monica will own the test harness and load generation; Lauren will coordinate resource allocation (dedicated instances vs hosted).

Proposed concrete timeline:
- Tue 5/5: Acme shares prompt templates + traffic profile (you said EOD)
- Wed 5/6: Redwood runs a smoke check (short, single-node) to validate test harness
- Thu–Fri 5/7–5/8: Full-scale 48h run (sustained window, plus 4 spike windows)
- Mon 5/11: Results, per-template breakdown, and suggested config for production (canary sizing + cache settings)

If that schedule looks OK I'll book the test cluster and share the runbook link.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachments: none
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthish Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 May 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme MAP loadtest plan and infra ask

Lauren / Markus — quick internal note to align infra.

Run details (per Karthik / Acme prompts):
- Workload mix: 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65–512 tokens), 10% long (>512 tokens)
- Target concurrency profile: baseline 30 rps, peak bursts to 120 rps for 5-minute windows every hour
- Context window for long prompts: 8k tokens

Infra ask: reserve two c5-dedicated pods (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) for Thu–Fri 5/7–5/8; enable KV prefix caching and quantized model variant for throughput run. We'll collect TTFT, p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, and 5xx counts.

I'll instrument the harness to output per-template CSVs and a reproducibility report (50-run latency stdev). Markus, can you confirm GPU reservation and assist with kernel-selection flags?

—Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthish Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eli Tanner <eli.tanner@acmecorp.com>, Samira Gomez <samira.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP benchmark results & next steps (attached)

Eli / Samira — thanks for the collaboration. We completed the 48h run and the reproducibility batch. Summary highlights (full CSV attached: loadtest-results-20260510.csv):

- Median TTFT: 92 ms (across all templates)
- P95 token latency: 238 ms; P99 token latency: 412 ms (long-template-heavy windows drove P99)
- Sustained throughput: 125 req/min with 0.6% 5xx errors during two short infra interruptions (post-mitigation below)
- Reproducibility: 50-run per-template stdev of TTFT <= 12% for all templates (meets Acme request <15%)

Notes / recommended changes:
- For long-template-heavy traffic, enable the quantized variant plus auto-prefix caching to keep P99 <350 ms.
- We observed a brief network blip on Fri 5/8 that caused the 5xx spike; we've implemented a retry/backoff policy and a routing fallback to a secondary AZ for the next run.

Next steps:
- Karthik: propose production canary sizing (two small dedicated pods + one burst pool) — target this week
- Acme: confirm whether you want the quantized config in prod or prefer conservative (higher-precision) outputs; we'll provide quality regression checks tied to your eval prompts.

Attachments: loadtest-results-20260510.csv (CSV, per-template rows)

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
